title: Grade 7 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Nutrition in Animals — Day 2 of 5: The digestive system
subject: science

questions.question: The correct order of organs in the human digestive system is:
options: Mouth → Oesophagus → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine
Mouth → Small intestine → Stomach → Large intestine
questions.explanation: Food travels: Mouth → Oesophagus (food pipe) → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine → Anus.

questions.question: Which acid is produced in the stomach to help digestion?
questions.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid (HCl) which creates an acidic environment needed for pepsin to digest proteins and also kills bacteria.

questions.question: What is peristalsis?
options: The breakdown of food by enzymes
Wave-like muscle contractions that push food along the digestive tract
Mixing of food with digestive juices
questions.explanation: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the oesophagus and intestines that pushes food forward.

questions.question: What is the function of bile in digestion?
options: Emulsifies (breaks up) fats into smaller droplets
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats — it breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones so that fat-digesting enzymes (lipase) can work better.

questions.question: Where is bile stored before it is released into the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Bile is produced in the liver and stored in the gall bladder. When needed, it flows into the small intestine.

questions.question: Which digestive gland produces insulin and digestive enzymes?
questions.explanation: The pancreas is a dual-function gland: it produces digestive enzymes (protease, lipase, amylase) and also the hormone insulin.

questions.question: What is chyme?
options: The semi-liquid mixture of food and gastric juices in the stomach
questions.explanation: Chyme is the semi-liquid, acidic mixture that forms when stomach muscles churn food with gastric juices.

questions.question: Digestion of carbohydrates BEGINS in the:
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth begins starch digestion, breaking it into smaller sugars (maltose).

questions.question: The enzyme pepsin digests:
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protease enzyme in the stomach that breaks protein molecules into shorter chains (peptides).

questions.question: Nutrients are absorbed into the bloodstream mainly in the:
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the main absorption site. Digested nutrients pass through villi into blood capillaries.

questions.question: What is the role of the large intestine?
options: Absorbing water and forming solid waste
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested material, compacting it into faeces for elimination.

questions.question: The finger-like projections (villi) in the small intestine help in:
options: Increasing surface area for better absorption
questions.explanation: Villi massively increase the surface area of the small intestine, allowing faster and more efficient absorption of nutrients.

questions.question: Which part of the digestive system absorbs WATER?
questions.explanation: The large intestine is where most water is reabsorbed. This is why faeces are solid rather than liquid.

questions.question: Egestion (defecation) is:
options: Removal of undigested solid waste through the anus
questions.explanation: Egestion is the elimination of undigested waste (faeces) through the anus at the end of the digestive process.

questions.question: What makes the stomach wall resistant to being digested by its own acid?
options: A layer of mucus secreted by the stomach lining
questions.explanation: Mucus secreted by the stomach lining protects it from being damaged by its own hydrochloric acid and enzymes.
